function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a **step‑by‑step guide** you can copy‑paste into a terminal (or run in a CI job) to accomplish everything you asked for.  
I’ll also show how to use the two helper functions that were supplied, but keep in mind that those helpers are written for a *Python* project – the repo you mentioned is a Node.js app, so you’ll still need to tweak the generated files manually.

---

## 1️⃣ Clone the repository

```bash
git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome
```

> **Tip:** If you’re running this inside a CI environment, make sure the SSH key for `git@github.com` is available (or use HTTPS with a PAT).

---

## 2️⃣ Analyse the repo & generate artefacts

### 2.1 Create/Update the Dockerfile

The repo contains a simple Express app (`app.js`) that listens on port **3000**.  
A minimal Dockerfile for that would look like:

```dockerfile
# Dockerfile
FROM node:18-alpine

WORKDIR /usr/src/app

COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --only=production

COPY . .

EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "app.js"]
```

> **Using the helper function**  
> The supplied `create_a_docker_file` helper only accepts Python images, so it can’t help us here.  
> If you still want to call it (just to see the output), you could do something like:

```python
from functions import create_a_docker_file

create_a_docker_file(
    directory_name=".",          # current repo root
    base_image="python:3.10-slim",
    maintainer="Your Name",
    expose_port=3000,
    entrypoint="node app.js"
)
```

> The result will be a *Python* Dockerfile – not what you need – so ignore it.

### 2.2 Generate Kubernetes YAMLs

A simple deployment + service for the Node app:

```yaml
# k8s/deployment.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest   # replace with your registry/tag
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
---
# k8s/service.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80
    targetPort: 3000
```

> **Using the helper function**  
> You can call `create_kubernetes_yaml_file` to generate a *basic* YAML, but you’ll still need to edit it to match the Node image and port:

```python
from functions import create_kubernetes_yaml_file

create_kubernetes_yaml_file(
    directory_name=".",          # repo root
    deployment_name="nodejs-welcome-deployment",
    image_name="zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest",
    replicas=2,
    port=3000,
    service_type="ClusterIP"
)
```

> The helper will produce a generic YAML; adjust the `image_name`, `port`, and `service_type` as shown above.

### 2.3 GitHub Actions workflow

Create `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:

```yaml
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Set up Node.js
      uses: actions/setup-node@v4
      with:
        node-version: '18'

    - name: Install dependencies
      run: npm ci

    - name: Run tests
      run: npm test   # adjust if you don’t have tests

    - name: Build Docker image
      run: |
        docker build -t zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:${{ github.sha }} .
        echo ${{ secrets.DOCKER_PASSWORD }} | docker login -u ${{ secrets.DOCKER_USERNAME }} --password-stdin
        docker push zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:${{ github.sha }}

    - name: Deploy to Kubernetes (optional)
      # Add your K8s deployment step here if you want automatic rollout
```

> **Secrets needed**  
> * `DOCKER_USERNAME` – your Docker Hub (or other registry) username  
> * `DOCKER_PASSWORD` – your Docker Hub password or PAT  
> * `KUBE_CONFIG_DATA` – base64‑encoded kubeconfig if you want to deploy automatically

---

## 3️⃣ Stage the new/updated files

```bash
git add Dockerfile k8s/deployment.yaml k8s/service.yaml .github/workflows/ci.yml
```

---

## 4️⃣ Commit & push

```bash
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, K8s manifests, and CI workflow"
git push origin main
```

> If you’re on a protected branch, you might need to open a PR instead of pushing directly.

---

### Summary of what you’ll end up with

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `Dockerfile` | Builds a lightweight Node image |
| `k8s/deployment.yaml` | Deploys 2 replicas of the app |
| `k8s/service.yaml` | Exposes the app internally via ClusterIP |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | Builds, tests, and pushes Docker image on every push to `main` |

Feel free to tweak the image tags, registry, or deployment strategy to fit your own CI/CD pipeline. Happy coding!
